primitives.name: Functional Principal Components Analysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Methodology** We modeled athlete aging curves using functional data analysis.
primitives.latex: \text{Let } X_i(t) \text{ be the performance function for athlete } i \text{ at age } t.\text{ FPCA seeks functions } \phi_k(t) \text{ and scores } a_{ik} \text{ minimizing } \sum_i \int \left(X_i(t) - \mu(t) - \sum_{k=1}^K a_{ik}\phi_k(t)\right)^2 dt,\text{ where } \mu(t) = E[X_i(t)].

primitives.assumptions: Assumes that individual athlete trajectories lie in a low-dimensional functional subspace. Requires sufficient longitudinal data per athlete.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Poor performance when data sparsity exceeds the intrinsic rank of the underlying process.

primitives.name: Informatively Missing Functional Principal Components Analysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: Clustering was then performed on the percent change of World Athletics points, at both the population and event level, to group athletes with similar developmental trajectories.
primitives.latex: \text{Define } T_i = \text{last observed age for athlete } i.\text{ imFunPCA maximizes } \sum_i \int_0^{T_i} \left(X_i(t) - \hat{\mu}(t) - \sum_{k=1}^K \hat{a}_{ik}\phi_k(t)\right)^2 dt \text{ subject to } \hat{X}_i(t) \leq X_i(T_i) \text{ for all } t > T_i.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is extracting latent developmental patterns from sparse, irregularly sampled performance data while correcting for selection bias. Functional Principal Components Analysis (FPCA) provides a dimensionality reduction framework that captures dominant modes of variation in athlete trajectories. However, standard FPCA suffers from right-tail selection bias because elite athletes who drop out tend to do so after reaching their best performances. Informatively Missing FPCA (imFunPCA) addresses this by imposing a monotonicity constraint post-dropout, ensuring that predicted performance never exceeds the terminal observation. This constraint can be interpreted as a form of conformal prediction under a monotone response model, linking our method to GSI's uncertainty quantification pipeline. Clustering the resulting percent-change trajectories reveals distinct developmental archetypes—early risers, late bloomers, etc.—which can be mapped to GSE's multi-armed bandit framework for personalized resource allocation. The career progression histogram serves as a sanity check, showing the distribution of performance ages across the population. Together, these operators form a unified pipeline from functional smoothing to predictive stratification, enabling accurate forecasting of when athletes will reach elite thresholds.
